finding.claim: The avatar endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL server-side. The only check is that the URL starts with https://. There is no host or IP allowlist, no private-range blocking and no DNS-rebinding protection. An attacker can make the server request internal HTTPS services, such as https://users.internal, internal admin endpoints or other private hosts. Cloud metadata endpoints are reachable only if they serve HTTPS or are reached through a redirect. axios follows redirects by default, so an attacker-controlled https:// host can 302 to http://169.254.169.254/ or http://users.internal:8080/ and bypass the scheme check. The response is not returned, but the byte length is, which gives a blind oracle for probing internal hosts, and any side-effecting GET endpoints can be triggered.

trace.note: Only checks typeof string and startsWith('https://')
axios.get(url) issues the request with default redirect following
The response size is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: The https:// prefix check at line 11 does not restrict the host or IP. There is no allowlist, no private or loopback or link-local IP blocking, no DNS resolution check and no maxRedirects:0 setting. There is no authentication middleware. I also reviewed GET /users/:id (lines 18-22). It is not reported as SSRF because the host is fixed to USER_SVC and the id is passed through encodeURIComponent, so it cannot change the host or scheme.

verdict.guard_found: none (only typeof string and startsWith('https://') at server.js:11, which is a prefix/scheme-only check; no auth middleware, no host allowlist, no maxRedirects:0)
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl from an unauthenticated JSON body, server.js:11 applies only a scheme-prefix check, and server.js:14 passes it to axios.get with default redirect following, so internal hosts are reachable and server.js:15 returns the byte length.
